title: Wittmann wins Misano Race 1 from last on the grid
dek: Marco Wittmann won Misano Race 1 for BMW from 18th on the grid, pitting at the end of lap one and finishing 8.2 seconds clear of pole-sitter René Rast.

chapters.title: A third round on the Adriatic with two outside names
text: The DTM came to Misano World Circuit on 8–9 June for the third round of 2019, with two races in two days. BMW’s Philipp Eng arrived as championship leader after the opening rounds at Hockenheim and Zolder, driving the #25 BMW Team RMR M4 DTM.

Misano is a high-speed circuit that punishes tyres, and the heat made it more demanding. Hankook expected a one-stop race, every driver had seven sets of slicks for the weekend, and the mandatory pit stop meant the real question was when to take it.

The entry list had two unfamiliar names. Jamie Green was unwell, and Pietro Fittipaldi stood in for him after strong performances in his first two DTM events, which Audi Sport head Dieter Gass called the best solution on short notice. Andrea Dovizioso, the Ducati MotoGP rider, made a one-off guest appearance in a WRT-run Audi in his home country, after a test at Misano coached by two-time champion Mattias Ekström. Daniel Juncadella of R-Motorsport, whose Aston Martin team had struggled for pace in its first DTM season, joked on Friday that the MotoGP rider could worry his team: “I could worry about him.”

chapters.title: Rast takes pole with one run and an Audi top four
text: René Rast set 1:25.294 on his first run in the Audi Sport Team Rosberg car, then stayed in the garage while the rest of the field improved. High tyre wear in the hot conditions was part of the thinking, and nobody inside the top ten bettered their position on a second run. It was his first pole of the 2019 season, worth three points, and he said afterwards that saving the tyres was the better option.

Jonathan Aberdein put the WRT Audi on the front row, 0.068 seconds behind, the best qualifying performance of the year for a team that had made its DTM debut this season. Loïc Duval was third and Robin Frijns fourth, completing an Audi lockout of the top four. Sheldon van der Linde, the Zolder pole-sitter, was the fastest BMW in fifth, ahead of Bruno Spengler and Eng. Nico Müller, Mike Rockenfeller and Timo Glock took eighth to tenth, with Fittipaldi 11th and Joel Eriksson 12th.

Jake Dennis was the best of the R-Motorsport Aston Martins in 13th, and Juncadella, 14th, qualified ahead of Dovizioso, who was 15th and about 1.7 seconds off Rast’s time. Ferdinand Habsburg and Paul di Resta were 16th and 17th. Marco Wittmann, a two-time champion, never set a timed lap: engine trouble kept the Team RMG BMW in the garage while mechanics worked on it, and he would start 18th and last.

chapters.title: A gamble on lap one and a safety car on lap three
text: Rast led away from pole, but Aberdein made a poor start and dropped behind Duval and Spengler, who had made up places from sixth on the grid. At the end of the first lap Wittmann dived into the pits for his mandatory stop, and Habsburg’s Aston Martin followed him, so both were committing to nearly the whole race on a single set of tyres. Wittmann was betting on a safety car.

He got one. Eriksson’s RBM BMW stopped on the track at Turn 7 on lap three, and the safety car stayed out for three laps, adding two laps to the race. That turned an early stop into a nearly free one. After the restart Rast kept the lead from Duval, van der Linde passed Spengler at Turn 1 before Spengler took the place back two corners later, and Frijns passed Aberdein for fifth on lap ten.

chapters.title: Wittmann inherits the lead as the field stops
text: Wittmann worked his way into the top ten within the first 13 laps and was seventh by lap 14, the first of the drivers who had already stopped. Rast came in at the end of lap 15, followed by Spengler and Frijns. Frijns’s Audi would not restart after the tyre change, and the delay effectively ended his race.

Rast rejoined about 20 seconds behind Wittmann, and his engineer told him over the radio they did not believe the BMW could reach the end without another stop. When everyone had stopped, Wittmann led from Habsburg, with Rast third and roughly 27 seconds back, though the Audi was initially lapping about two seconds faster than the leader and some four faster than the Aston Martin.

chapters.title: Rast closes to 8.2 seconds but runs out of laps
text: Rast had to clear Habsburg first, and did so on lap 27 after Habsburg got a poor exit from the fast Turn 10. In clear air he took more than 20 seconds out of Wittmann’s lead over the second stint, but the gap was still 8.238 seconds at the flag. Wittmann had worried about the final five or six laps as his tyres faded, yet the gamble held and gave him his second win of the season.

Duval completed the podium, 17.686 seconds back, after passing Habsburg on lap 30 as the Aston Martin’s tyres dropped away; Habsburg ended up 14th. Spengler was fourth, Müller edged Rockenfeller for fifth and sixth on matching strategies, and Eng was seventh after a late duel with team-mate van der Linde, who finished ninth behind Aberdein, eighth after a poor start and a delayed stop. Glock was tenth.

Fittipaldi was 11th and Dovizioso 12th on his DTM debut, seven seconds behind Fittipaldi and ahead of the Aston Martins of Juncadella, Habsburg and Dennis. Di Resta stopped with about eight laps to go, while Frijns and Eriksson did not finish.

facts.v: Wittmann started 18th after engine trouble stopped him setting a timed lap, then won by 8.238 seconds from Rast.
